newsitem.title: MACAU: China gives assurances on Macau rights -Portugal.
newsitem.headline: China gives assurances on Macau rights -Portugal.

text.p: Portuguese President Jorge Sampaio received assurances from Chinese leaders on Tuesday that Beijing would respect human rights after it takes over Macau in 1999.

"The Chinese side reaffirmed that the (legal) guarantees of the citizens, civil rights and liberties in force in Macau will be respected after 1999," Sampaio told Macau-based reporters travelling with him in China.
The Portuguese-run enclave reverts to Chinese rule on December 20, 1999, two and a half years after the neighbouring British colony of Hong Kong.
Sampaio said China's "respect for the liberties in force in Macau" would constitute a "very positive contribution" towards the human rights dialogue between Europe and China.
"Even President Jiang Zemin said that," Sampaio was quoted as saying at the press conference on Tuesday morning.
Sampaio met with Jiang at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing on Monday.
Sampaio also said Lisbon and Beijing had agreed to speed up the work of the Sino-Portuguese Joint Liaison Group (JLG) responsible for handling details of Macau's return to China.
He was quoted as saying the 10-member JLG should meet more than the current three times a year.
"The breaks between the meetings are very long," he said, adding that "the Chinese president thinks that the meetings should take place more often".
The lead-up to Macau's transition has been markedly smooth, unlike Hong Kong's, as the Portuguese have sought Beijing's approval on all major policy decisions and infrastructure projects.
